newsitem.title: CHINA: Hongkong Bank sees HK GDP growing 5.4 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Bank sees HK GDP growing 5.4 pct in 1997.

text.p: Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd said on Thursday that it expects Hong Kong to achieve real gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.4 percent in 1997, while inflation is forecast to rise by 6.4 percent.
The new forecasts were updated from the bank's preliminary forecasts of 5.2 percent GDP growth and 6.8 percent inflation made in December.
GDP grew 4.7 percent in 1996, while the Consumer Price Index (A) rose 6.0 percent, the bank said.
Hongkong Bank said the territory's economy performed strongly in the first half of 1997, driven mainly by robust domestic demand.
Buoyed by rising property and stock prices, private consumption expanded rapidly, while investment spending also benefited from increased private construction activity.
In contrast, growth in Hong Kong's external trade remains sluggish due to weak overseas demand, the bank said.
The bank said the strong momentum in domestic demand is expected to continue in the second half.

Although there is some uncertainty in the property market following the government's announcement of its intention to tackle speculation and restrain rising property prices, the upward thrust should not be severely affected, it said.
Only a mild adjustment in the property market is anticipated, provided that no drastic interventionist measures are introduced, it said.

Hongkong Bank said external trade should improve in the coming months due to stronger overseas demand, but the level is not expected to be enough to revive Hong Kong's trade figures to any great extent.
As a result, Hong Kong's growth momentum will continue to be derived from the domestic sector, it said.
While inflation was suppressed sharply in the first half by declining food prices, with CPI(A) at 5.9 percent, it was likely to edge higher in the second half with strong domestic activity, it said.
